```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 90, message = FALSE)
has_mvln <- requireNamespace("mvtnorm", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)
library(ss3diags2)
library(ggplot2)
```

The Stock Synthesis assessment of northern shrimp (*Pandalus borealis*) in Skagerrak and the Norwegian Deep
(pra.27.3a4a, SS 3.30.22, 1970-2024) uses most of the structure SS3 offers:

* four seasons (quarters), spawning in season 1;
* two sexes with protandric hermaphroditism: shrimp are born male and change to female;
* two areas (1: Skagerrak 3.a, 2: Norwegian Deep 4.a) with time-varying recruitment distribution;
* six area-specific fleets (Denmark, Norway, Sweden in each area) with seasonal catches, retention and discards, and
  two surveys with sex-specific length compositions;
* F reported as Fbar over ages 1-3 (Z - M) and an MSY proxy of F at B30%.

The report (with the CoVar table reduced to the derived quantities) and the SS3 input files ship with the package.

```{r data}
dir <- system.file("extdata", "pra.27.3a4a", package = "ss3diags2")
pra <- readRDS(file.path(dir, "pra.27.3a4a.rds"))
ss3_fleets(pra)
```

# Part I: structure

# 1. How the structure maps to FLR

| SS3                  | FLR dimension | note                                                         |
|----------------------|---------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| sex (data Sexes 1-3) | unit          | "F", "M"; combined-sex data (Sexes 0) stay "unique"          |
| season               | season        | seasons stay seasons (not years)                             |
| area                 | area          | the area of the fleet; fleets are area-specific              |
| partition 0/1/2      | fleet name    | `fleet.all`, `fleet.discard`, `fleet.retained`               |
| morph / platoon      | (averaged)    | in F-at-age and selectivity                                  |

Because each fleet fishes in one area, the observations need no area split: the area is a property of the fleet.

# 2. Observations by season, sex and area

```{r catch, fig.height = 7}
ct <- ss3_catch(pra)
ss3plot_catch(ct, by = c("season", "area"))
```

```{r comps, fig.height = 7}
lfd <- ss3_lencomp(pra)
names(lfd)
ss3plot_comps(lfd, fit = ss3_lencomp(pra, what = "exp"), fleets = c("NORSURVEY3a", "NORSURVEY4a"), by = "unit")
ss3plot_comps(lfd, type = "mean", by = "season", fleets = c("DK3a", "NOR3a", "SWE3a"))
```

OSA residuals of the survey length compositions by sex with cohort tracks of growth for both sexes (the model uses
the same growth for both):

```{r osa, fig.height = 6}
lh <- ss3_lhpar(pra)
rs <- ss3_resid(pra, fleets = c("NORSURVEY3a", "NORSURVEY4a"))
ss3plot_resid(rs, lhpar = lh)
```

# 3. Selectivity, retention and the stock by area

```{r sel, fig.height = 7}
ss3plot_sel(ss3_sel(pra), ret = ss3_sel(pra, "ret"))
```

```{r byarea, fig.height = 7}
ba <- ss3_byarea(pra)                       # FLQuants SSB, B, Rec with an area dimension
ss3plot_byarea(ba)
ss3plot_byarea(ba, type = "share")
```

# Part II: management quantities

`ss3plot()` summarises the assessment on one page, as the JABBA3 summary plot: SSB (with the observed indices
scaled to SSB), F and catch with reference points, B/Btgt, F/Ftgt and the Kobe plot (here with F(y) against
B(y + 1), see section 5), the stock-recruitment curve, the recruitment deviations and the production phase plot.

```{r ss3plot, eval = has_mvln && requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9.5}
ss3plot(pra, iters = 500, lag = 1)
```

# 4. Stock status: FLStockR and MVLN

`ss3stk()` builds the simplified `FLStockR` of `FLRef::ss2FLStockR()`: maximum likelihood estimates with standard
errors (`output = "mle"`), or draws from a multivariate lognormal (MVLN) approximation (`output = "iters"`,
`ss3mvln()`).

* `ss3mvln(method = "joint")` (default) draws SSB, recruitment and F of all years and the reference points from one
  MVLN with the full correlation matrix of the SS3 derived quantities (Kell et al. 2023; the `ss3om::ssmvln()`
  approach). Each iteration is a coherent trajectory and the reference points have iterations.
* `ss3mvln(method = "annual")` is the delta-MVLN of `ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN()` (Walter and Winker 2020;
  Winker et al. 2019), drawn year by year.

```{r mvln, eval = has_mvln, fig.height = 7}
stk <- ss3stk(pra, output = "iters", iters = 500, fwd = TRUE)
ss3plot_trj(stk)
```

**Note on SSdeltaMVLN.** For the example models the year-by-year delta-MVLN understates the correlation between
B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy in the terminal year (shortfin mako: -0.24, against -0.86 in the SS3 covariance; Pacific hake:
-0.26 against -0.76), so its Kobe clouds are rounder than the estimated uncertainty. The joint method keeps the
estimated correlation. Use `method = "joint"` for advice.

# 5. Kobe plots and the timing of F and SSB  {#kobe-lag}

> **Critical for advice.** SS3 reports SSB at spawning (typically at the start of the year), and F of year *y* acts
> during year *y*. The SSB that results from the fishing in year *y* is therefore SSB in year *y + 1*. The usual Kobe
> plot pairs F(*y*) with SSB(*y*): it shows the biomass the fishery in *y* started from, not the biomass it led to.
> When F is well above Fmsy, the stock status that follows from the current exploitation can be markedly worse
> than the plot of F(*y*) against SSB(*y*) suggests. Advice should state which convention is used and, when the
> two differ, show both.

`ss3plot_kobe(lag = 1)` plots F(*y*) against B/Btgt(*y + 1*). The uncertainty cloud then pairs F(*Y*) with B(*Y + 1*)
within each iteration, which needs draws linked across years: use `ss3mvln(method = "joint")` (a warning is given for
year-by-year draws). Build the stock with `fwd = TRUE` so that SSB at the start of the year after the last assessment
year (reported by SS3 as a forecast quantity) is available; F is used up to the end year only.

```{r kobe, eval = has_mvln, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
k0 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk) + ggtitle("lag = 0: F(y) against B(y)")
k1 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk, lag = 1) + ggtitle("lag = 1: F(y) against B(y + 1)")
if(requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) patchwork::wrap_plots(k0, k1) else k1
```

For North Atlantic shortfin mako the probability of being overfished and subject to overfishing (red quadrant) in
2015 is about 78% with F(2015) against SSB(2015) and about 93% with F(2015) against SSB(2016).

Points to check before using the lagged plot for advice:

* SSB(*y + 1*) for the last assessment year is a one-year forecast: it depends on the SS3 forecast settings
  (`forecast.ss`) and, where recruits mature within a year, on the forecast recruitment.
* Kell et al. (2023) pair F and SSB both ways in their figures (F in 2020 with SSB in 2021, and both in 2022); the
  convention is not standardised, which is why it must be stated with the advice.

# 6. Production function and equilibrium

`ss3_spm()` fits a Pella-Tomlinson production function to the SS3 equilibrium yield curve and checks it against
the SS3 benchmarks. SS3 holds several "unfished" states: SSB_Virgin (start-year biology), SSB_unfished (benchmark
years) and the dynamic B0 of each year; with time-varying weight-at-age or M (empirical `wtatage`) these differ, and
the equilibrium table can rest on yet another biology. `ss3_spm()` warns when its fit and the SS3 benchmarks differ. For northern shrimp the MSY proxy is F at B30%, not
the SS3 MSY, and the fitted production function differs from the benchmarks.

```{r spm}
stk1 <- ss3stk(pra)
ss3plot_production(stk1)
```

# 7. Fishing mortality at age, partial F and F by area

`ss3_fa()` returns F-at-age by fleet with the full structure (age, year, unit, season, area). F-at-age is on an
annual scale within each season; `annual = TRUE` sums the seasons weighted by their duration.

```{r fa, fig.height = 6}
fa <- ss3_fa(pra)
dimnames(fa[["NOR4a"]])[c("unit", "season", "area")]
ss3plot_fa(fa)
```

Partial F splits the reported F (Fbar 1-3) among fleets, gears or countries by their catch in numbers over the F
ages, so it adds up to F:

```{r partialF}
countries <- list(Denmark = c("DK3a", "DK4a"), Norway = c("NOR3a", "NOR4a"), Sweden = c("SWE3a", "SWE4a"))
pf <- ss3_partialF(pra, groups = countries)
ss3plot_partialF(pf)
ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra), type = "line")
```

Two notions of F by area should not be confused. Partial F by area (`groups = "area"`, `method = "catch"`) is each
area's share of the stock F. The F experienced by the fish in an area (`method = "fbar"`, the Fbar of the fleets of
that area) does not add up to the stock F when the stock is spread over the areas:

```{r Farea}
ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra, groups = "area"))
ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra, groups = "area", method = "fbar"))
ss3plot_partialF(ss3_partialF(pra, groups = countries, method = "apical", season = TRUE))
```

# 8. Partial impact on the spawning stock

`ss3_impact()` follows Wang et al. (2009): SSB is projected without fishing and with the fleet groups added one by
one, so the impact of a group is the SSB it removes, and all impacts add up to the dynamic B0 minus SSB. It runs on
the SS3 report, without re-running SS3: annual total mortality comes from the SS3 numbers at age (seasons, areas and
sexes pooled), fishing mortality Z - M is split among fleets by their catch at age, spawning output at age and the
recruitment deviations are those of SS3, and the start of each scenario is scaled by the initial equilibrium under
the initial F of its fleets. The projection with all fleets reproduces the SS3 SSB and the projection without fishing
reproduces the SS3 dynamic B0:

```{r impact}
imp <- ss3_impact(pra, groups = countries)
imp
head(imp$check)
ss3plot_impact(imp)
ss3plot_impact(imp, type = "prop")
ss3plot_impact(ss3_impact(pra, groups = "area"))
```

The order in which the groups are added matters for the share of each group when the stock-recruit relationship is
not flat; `type = "remove"` gives the loss of SSB caused by each group with all others fishing.
